claim: The paper proposes a two-level deployment policy for a cross-sectional LightGBM ranker: a strategy-level regime-trust gate G(t) that decides whether to trade at all (AUROC around 0.72 overall and 0.75 in the 2024 FINAL holdout period), and a position-level epistemic tail-risk cap that reduces exposure only for the most uncertain individual predictions.
quote: a strategy-level regime-trust gate G(t) that decides whether to trade (AUROC around 0.72 overall and 0.75 in FINAL) and a position-level epistemic tail-risk cap that reduces exposure only for the most uncertain predictions
limitations: Abstract-only reading (full text/method section paywalled at this URL by design of arXiv abstract pages; only the abstract was independently opened this session, not the full PDF's methods section with exact formulas). The paper's own universe/asset class and cost assumptions are not disclosed in the abstract. Numbers (AUROC 0.72/0.75) are the paper's own model and data, not a same-instrument replication on our T1 book.
impact_on_spec: Defines the regime-trust gate concept and its reported AUROC as the source motivating candidates U1/U2's exposure-cut mechanism; this iteration's own gate is a distinct, locally-trained implementation (bootstrap-ensemble disagreement on our own features/book), not a reproduction of the paper's exact model.

claim: The paper adapts Direct Epistemic Uncertainty Prediction (DEUP) to ranking by predicting rank displacement and defining an epistemic uncertainty signal ehat relative to a point-in-time-safe baseline; ehat's median correlation with absolute rank-score error is about 0.6 across 1,865 dates, and ehat is structurally coupled with signal strength, so naive inverse-uncertainty position sizing de-levers the strongest signals and degrades performance.
quote: We adapt Direct Epistemic Uncertainty Prediction (DEUP) to ranking by predicting rank displacement and defining an epistemic uncertainty signal ehat relative to a point-in-time (PIT-safe) baseline
limitations: Exact ehat construction (rank-displacement prediction model, its own training target) is in the paper's methods section, not the abstract; this iteration's own DEUP-style analogue (ensemble standard deviation of bootstrap LightGBM cross-sectional rank predictions, per candidate U3) is a standard, disclosed simplification -- ensemble disagreement as an epistemic-uncertainty proxy -- not a literal reimplementation of the paper's own rank-displacement predictor.
impact_on_spec: Directly motivates using ensemble disagreement (bootstrap standard deviation of cross-sectional rank predictions) as this iteration's u_i(t) epistemic-uncertainty proxy, and motivates testing U3 (an individual-name DEUP-style cap) as functionally different from U1/U2 (strategy-level gates), consistent with the paper's own finding that naive inverse-uncertainty sizing on the strongest signals is harmful.

claim: In the paper's own 'AI Stock Forecaster' setting, a LightGBM cross-sectional ranker performs well overall at a 20-day horizon, but the 2024 holdout period coincides with an AI thematic rally and sector rotation that breaks the signal at longer horizons and weakens the 20-day signal specifically.
quote: a LightGBM ranker performs well overall at a 20-day horizon, yet the 2024 holdout coincides with an AI thematic rally and sector rotation that breaks the signal at longer horizons and weakens 20d
limitations: The paper's asset universe, cost model and exact AI-rotation dates are not given in the abstract; the mechanism (2024 AI-rally regime break at a 20-day horizon for a LightGBM ranker) is stated as independent corroborating evidence for our own already-diagnosed problem (T1 book 2024+ drawdown), not as a same-instrument replication.
impact_on_spec: This is the direct motivation named in the queue task and registry row for testing a trained regime-trust/uncertainty gate on our own T1 20-session momentum book, which shares the 20-day-horizon, 2024-regime-break pattern the paper reports on its own ranker.
